section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse
section_1.content: Before understanding measures, one must understand the 'Beat'. Introduce the heartbeat analogy to establish the idea of a constant, recurring time unit.
section_1.example: A digital heartbeat monitor on screen showing a steady, rhythmic pulse (thump-thump) represented by glowing dots.

section_2.title: The Bar Line: Organizing the Chaos
section_2.content: Explain that music is divided into equal chunks called 'measures' (or bars) separated by vertical bar lines. This helps musicians organize the flow of rhythm.
section_2.example: A series of dots moving across the screen; a vertical wall (bar line) appears every 4th dot to group them into clear, distinct packets.

section_3.title: Time Signature: The Mathematical Blueprint
section_3.content: Introduce the time signature (e.g., 4/4). The top number tells us how many beats fit in a measure; the bottom number defines the 'value' of the beat.
section_3.example: A robotic conductor 'Chef' adding exactly 4 musical ingredients (notes) into a mixing bowl (measure) before closing the lid with a bar line.

section_4.title: Visualizing Fractions in Time
section_4.content: Use a graphical pie-chart representation to explain note values. A whole note is the whole circle, a half note is a semi-circle, etc., summing up to the measure total.
section_4.example: A circular 'clock' that fills up with colorful wedges (notes) until it completes a full circle, triggering a 'measure complete' sound effect.

section_5.title: Application: The Marching Ants
section_5.content: Summarize by applying the measure theory to a dynamic scenario to ensure mastery.
section_5.example: A line of ants marching in time to a 4/4 beat. Every 4th ant wears a special 'Cap' (the first beat accent), demonstrating how measure theory creates the predictable structure of music.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)
